  "title": "Opportunity Analysis in Intelligence",

  "decider": "The DNI",

  "agent": "The DNI",
  "agent_role": "decide",
  "situation": "At the decision point, the DNI was considering whether intelligence analysis on important issues should remain confined to threat assessment or also address opportunities for advancing interests. Intelligence analysis had traditionally been kept separate from policy formulation, but policymakers and legislators found fact-only briefings inadequate and sought analytic insight relevant to policy advancement. Opportunity analysis was understood as identifying levers that could advance U.S. and shared interests, but it remained controversial within the intelligence community. Analytic managers feared policy suggestions could taint analysis, and some worried that crossing the boundary would compromise objectivity and integrity. The competing view was that well-developed analytic practice could preserve integrity while giving policymakers better-targeted analysis.",
  "question": "What should the DNI do about requiring opportunity analysis in intelligence analyses on important issues?",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "The traditional view treated intelligence analysis as a service to policymakers, not as a formulator of objectives, drafter of policy, or maker of plans.",

    },

      "id": "F3",

    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "Opportunity analysis remained uncomfortable and controversial in parts of the intelligence community.",

    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "Analytic managers worried that suggesting policy options would taint analysis and undermine its integrity.",

    {
      "id": "F6",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "A concern was that crossing the policy boundary could compromise analytic objectivity and integrity; the counterview was that the craft was mature enough to preserve integrity.",
